questions.chapter: Irrigation Fundamentals, Soil-Water-Plant Relations & Duty-Delta
questions.text: Define Duty ($D$), Delta ($\Delta$), and Base Period ($B$). Derive the fundamental relation: $\Delta = \frac{8.64 B}{D}$ where $\Delta$ is in meters, $B$ in days, and $D$ in hectares/cumec. Explain Consumptive Use (Evapotranspiration $ET_0$), Field Capacity ($FC$), Permanent Wilting Point ($PWP$), and Readily Available Moisture (RAM).

questions.chapter: Canal Design Theories (Kennedy & Lacey Silt Theories)
questions.text: Compare Kennedy's Silt Theory vs. Lacey's Regime Silt Theory for alluvial channel design. State Lacey's Regime Equations: Silt factor ($f = 1.76\sqrt{d_{mm}}$), Velocity ($V = \left(\frac{Q f^2}{140}\right)^{1/6}$), Hydraulic radius ($R = \frac{5}{2}\frac{V^2}{f}$), Wetted perimeter ($P = 4.75\sqrt{Q}$), and Bed slope ($S = \frac{f^{5/3}}{3340 Q^{1/6}}$). Design an alluvial irrigation channel using Lacey's theory for discharge $Q = 40\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$ and silt factor $f = 1.0$.

questions.chapter: Diversion Headworks, Weirs & Barrages (Bligh & Khosla Theories)
questions.text: Draw a neat plan layout of a Canal Diversion Headworks on an alluvial river. Label all components: Main Weir/Barrage, Under-sluices, Divide wall, Fish ladder, Canal head regulator, Silt excluder, Silt ejector, and Guide bunds. Explain their functions.

questions.chapter: Diversion Headworks, Weirs & Barrages (Bligh & Khosla Theories)
questions.text: Explain Subsurface Flow theories under hydraulic structures: Bligh's Creep Theory, Lane's Weighted Creep Theory, and Khosla's Theory of Independent Variables. Explain Khosla's corrections for: (a) Thickness of floor, (b) Mutual interference of cut-off piles, and (c) Slope of floor. Define Exit Gradient ($G_E = \frac{H}{d}\frac{1}{\pi\sqrt{\lambda}}$) and calculate exit gradient for a barrage floor.

questions.chapter: Canal Regulation Structures (Falls, Cross-Regulators, Head-Regulators)
questions.text: What is a Canal Fall (Drop)? Why and where are canal falls provided? Explain types of falls: Ogee fall, Vertical drop fall (Sarda type), Glacis fall (Montague / Inglis baffle fall).

questions.chapter: Cross Drainage Works (Aqueducts, Siphons) & Agricultural Drainage
questions.text: Classify Cross-Drainage Works: (1) Drainage below Canal (Aqueduct vs Syphon Aqueduct), (2) Canal below Drainage (Superpassage vs Canal Siphon), and (3) Canal and Drainage at same level (Level Crossing vs Inlet/Outlet). Explain design selection criteria based on High Flood Level (HFL) and Full Supply Level (FSL).

questions.chapter: Cross Drainage Works (Aqueducts, Siphons) & Agricultural Drainage
questions.text: Explain Waterlogging in agricultural lands (Causes, adverse effects on crop yield, preventive measures). Explain Design of Subsurface Tile Drainage Systems using Hooghoudt's Equation for drain spacing: $S^2 = \frac{4K(h_2^2 - h_1^2)}{q} + \frac{8K d h}{q}$.
